questions.prompt: The general urged us to defend ourselves against the barbarians.
questions.answer: Dux nōs hortātus est ut nōs contrā barbarōs dēfenderēmus.

questions.prompt: I gave you my sword, but you did not thank me.
questions.answer: Ego tibi gladium meum dedī, sed tū mihi grātiās nōn ēgistī.

questions.prompt: The queen loves herself more than her own people.
questions.answer: Rēgīna sē magis quam populum suum amat.

questions.prompt: The soldiers gathered around their leader and pledged themselves to him.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs circā ducem suum congregātī sē eī dēvōvērunt.

questions.prompt: Tell me the truth, and I will forgive you.
questions.answer: Dīc mihi vēritātem, et ego tibi ignōscam.

questions.prompt: The philosopher said that he himself did not fear death.
questions.answer: Philosophus dīxit sē ipsum mortem nōn timēre.

questions.prompt: Your words moved me, but they did not move your friends.
questions.answer: Verba tua mē mōvērunt, sed amīcōs tuōs nōn mōvērunt.

questions.prompt: The king carried his own scepter, which had been given to him by the gods.
questions.answer: Rēx sceptrum suum ferēbat, quod eī ā deīs datum erat.

questions.prompt: Follow me, for I will show you the way home.
questions.answer: Sequere mē, nam ego tibi viam domum mōnstrābō.

questions.prompt: Each of us defended his own city with great courage.
questions.answer: Uterque nostrum urbem suam magnā virtūte dēfendit.

questions.prompt: You all promised us that you would come to our aid.
questions.answer: Vōs pollicitī estis vōs nōbīs subventūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: We praised you because you had freed yourselves from slavery.
questions.answer: Nōs vōs laudāvimus quod vōs ē servitūte līberāverātis.

questions.prompt: Our leader ordered us to gather our weapons quickly.
questions.answer: Dux noster nōs iussit arma nostra celeriter colligere.

questions.prompt: The wise man knows himself and trusts his own judgment.
questions.answer: Vir sapiēns sē cognōscit et iūdiciō suō cōnfīdit.

questions.prompt: The mother embraced her son and pressed him to herself.
questions.answer: Māter fīlium amplexa est et eum ad sē pressit.

questions.prompt: The tyrant surrounded himself with guards, fearing for his own life.
questions.answer: Tyrannus sē custōdibus circumdedit, suae vītae timēns.

questions.prompt: I gave you my sword, but you never returned it to me.
questions.answer: Tibi gladium meum dedī, sed eum mihi numquam reddidistī.

questions.prompt: You praised me, but I do not trust your promises.
questions.answer: Mē laudāvistī, sed prōmissīs tuīs nōn crēdō.

questions.prompt: The god was propitious to us and gave us his own gifts.
questions.answer: Deus nōbīs propitius erat et dōna sua dedit.

questions.prompt: The freedwoman freed herself from fear and trusted her own talent.
questions.answer: Liberta sē metū līberāvit et ingeniō suō crēdidit.

questions.prompt: I will tell you what I saw with my own eyes.
questions.answer: Tibi dīcam quod meīs oculīs vīdī.

questions.prompt: The boy threw away his shield and fled to his friends.
questions.answer: Puer scūtum suum abjēcit et ad amīcōs suōs fūgit.

questions.prompt: We hid ourselves in the woods so that the enemy might not see us.
questions.answer: Nōs in silvīs cēlāvimus nē hostēs nōs vidērent.

questions.prompt: The poet praised himself too much, but his songs pleased me.
questions.answer: Poēta sē nimium laudāvit, sed carmina eius mihi placuērunt.

questions.prompt: Show me your wounds, for they frighten your mother.
questions.answer: Mihi vulnera tua ostende, nam mātrem tuam terrent.

questions.prompt: The woman promised herself that she would never abandon her children.
questions.answer: Fēmina sibi prōmīsit sē līberōs suōs numquam relictūram esse.

questions.prompt: You entrusted your money to me, and I kept it faithfully.
questions.answer: Pecūniam tuam mihi crēdidistī, et eam fidēliter servāvī.

questions.prompt: The soldiers hurled themselves upon the enemy with a great shout.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs magnō clāmōre sē in hostēs iēcērunt.

questions.prompt: I do not fear you, for the gods are on our side.
questions.answer: Tē nōn timeō, nam dī nōbīscum sunt.

questions.prompt: You all trusted your leader too much, and he betrayed you.
questions.answer: Ducī vestrō nimium crēdidistis, et vōs prōdidit.

questions.prompt: I prepared myself for the journey and took up my weapons.
questions.answer: Mē ad iter parāvī et arma mea sūmpsī.

questions.prompt: The girl looked at herself in the water and smiled.
questions.answer: Puella sē in aquā spectāvit et rīsit.

questions.prompt: Give me your hand, and I will lead you out of danger.
questions.answer: Mihi manum tuam dā, et tē ē perīculō ēdūcam.

questions.prompt: The queen praised herself, but she trusted no one else.
questions.answer: Rēgīna sē laudāvit, sed nēminī aliī crēdidit.

questions.prompt: You know that I gave you my whole heart.
questions.answer: Scīs mē tibi tōtum animum meum dedisse.

questions.prompt: We ourselves saw the enemy fleeing across the deep river.
questions.answer: Nōs ipsī hostēs trāns altum flūmen fugientēs vīdimus.

questions.prompt: Because you feared us, you hid your gold from your friends.
questions.answer: Quod nōs timēbās, aurum tuum ab amīcīs cēlāvistī.

questions.prompt: The old man, conscious of his own crime, could not forgive himself.
questions.answer: Senex, suī sceleris cōnscius, sibi ignōscere nōn poterat.

questions.prompt: The poet praised us, but you all envied our glory.
questions.answer: Poēta nōs laudāvit, sed vōs nostrae glōriae invidēbātis.

questions.prompt: The mother embraced her son and drew him to herself.
questions.answer: Māter fīlium amplexa est et eum ad sē trāxit.

questions.prompt: You promised me that you would tell me the truth.
questions.answer: Mihi pollicitus es tē mihi vēritātem dictūrum esse.

questions.prompt: The soldiers threw themselves before the king and begged for mercy.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs sē ante rēgem iēcērunt et veniam rogāvērunt.

questions.prompt: I trust you, but you yourself do not trust yourself.
questions.answer: Tibi crēdō, sed tū tibi ipse nōn crēdis.

questions.prompt: You can no longer stay among us; I will not bear it, I will not endure it, I will not allow it.
questions.answer: Nōbīscum versārī iam diūtius nōn potes; nōn feram, nōn patiar, nōn sinam.

questions.prompt: If you and the army are well, it is well.
questions.answer: Sī tū exercitusque valētis, bene est.

questions.prompt: Unless had lost it, I should not have recovered it.
questions.answer: Nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem.

questions.prompt: It would not have come into my mind unless reminded.
questions.answer: Nōn mihi, nisi admonitō, vēnisset in mentem.

questions.prompt: What harm will the mangling by wild beasts do me if I don't feel anything?
questions.answer: Quid igitur mihi ferārum laniātus oberit nihil sentientī.

questions.prompt: Do not doubt that I will do all.
questions.answer: Illud cavē dubitēs quīn ego omnia faciam.

questions.prompt: I doubt whether you will receive this very letter.
questions.answer: Dubitābam tū hās ipsās litterās essēsne acceptūrus.

questions.prompt: I think we must be allowed to use a Greek word.
questions.answer: Putō concēdī nōbīs oportēre ut Graecō verbō ūtāmur.

questions.prompt: For it had not happened to be necessary to me.
questions.answer: Nec enim acciderat mihi opus esse.

questions.prompt: I hope that will be our happy lot.
questions.answer: Spērō fore ut contingat id nōbīs.

questions.prompt: Consider whether you ought to have any hesitation.
questions.answer: vidēte num dubitandum vōbīs sit.

questions.prompt: In this one circumstance do we perhaps most of all surpass brutes, that we can talk with each other.
questions.answer: hōc ūnō praestāmus vel maximē ferīs, quod conloquimur inter nōs.

questions.prompt: It must be the case that you have made his acquaintance yourself.
questions.answer: fierī nōn potest ut eum tū nōn cōgnōverīs.

questions.prompt: I have no doubt about what you think is our duty to do.
questions.answer: nōn dubitō, quid nōbīs agendum putēs.

questions.prompt: Tell it at Sparta, friend, that thou hast seen us lying here, obedient to our country’s holy laws.
questions.answer: dīc, hospes, Spartae nōs tē hīc vīdisse iacentīs, dum sānctīs patriae lēgibus obsequimur.

questions.prompt: I am thinking of staying here till I feel better.
questions.answer: ego hīc cōgitō commorārī, quoad mē reficiam.
